html:
The eruption of Mount Pinatubo on the island of Luzon in the Philippines in June 1991, the second largest volcanic eruption of the 1900s. It cooled the whole planet for about two years.

The volcano had been quiet for about 500 years. In April 1991 steam blasts began. Philippine and American scientists from the US Geological Survey watched it closely and warned of a huge eruption. Tens of thousands of people were moved away, among them many Aeta, who lived on its slopes. Those warnings saved thousands of lives.

The climax came on 15 June, at the same time as a typhoon. Rain soaked the falling ash, and its weight collapsed roofs. Several hundred people died, most from this. For years afterwards, mudflows called lahars buried towns and fields. The United States abandoned nearby Clark Air Base.

The eruption sent millions of tonnes of sulphur dioxide high into the stratosphere. The haze spread around the globe and lowered average temperatures by about half a degree for a year or more, as Tambora had done far more severely in 1815.
sum: The eruption of Mount Pinatubo on the island of Luzon in the Philippines in June 1991, the second largest volcanic eruption of the 1900s. It cooled the whole planet for about two years.
